review.en: The first month of the First World War, from the plans laid years before to the Battle of the Marne, told as narrative with a novelist's command of character and pace. Tuchman shows how rigid plans, pride and misread signals carried Europe into a war no one had planned to fight that way. Specialists have questioned some emphases, but it remains a model of narrative history and won a Pulitzer Prize.
review.zh: 第一次世界大战的第一个月，从多年前定下的作战计划写到马恩河战役，叙事兼有小说家对人物和节奏的掌控。塔奇曼写出僵硬的计划、傲慢与误读的信号，怎样把欧洲拖进一场谁都没料到会这样打的战争。专家对其部分侧重有所质疑，但它仍是叙事史的典范，并获普利策奖。
